title: DIY or Call a Pro? Find Your Fix-It Style
intro: Answer 7 quick questions to see whether you're wired to tackle home repairs yourself or to hand them off to a pro. This is for fun and general guidance, not a safety certification.
disclaimer: This quiz is just for fun and general guidance, not a substitute for good judgment. Know your limits: certain jobs, especially anything involving gas lines, major electrical work, structural changes, or permits, should always go to a licensed, insured professional. When in doubt, call a pro.

questions.q: A cabinet door starts hanging crooked. Your first reaction?

options.t: Grab a screwdriver and adjust the hinge myself
Watch a quick video, then maybe try it
Add it to the list for the next handyman visit

questions.q: How do you feel about owning and using tools?

options.t: I've got a kit I actually know how to use
I own the basics but reach for them rarely
A hammer and a hopeful attitude, that's about it

questions.q: When something breaks, what motivates you most?

options.t: Saving money and the satisfaction of doing it myself
Getting it fixed, by whichever path is easiest
Just making the problem disappear quickly

questions.q: How's your patience with a project that fights back?

options.t: I'll troubleshoot for hours until I crack it
I'll give it a couple tries, then reassess
Frustration hits fast; I'd rather not

questions.q: How do you spend a free Saturday at home?

options.t: Knocking out a project on the to-do list
A small task if the mood strikes
Relaxing; chores can wait for someone else

questions.q: How comfortable are you learning a new skill from scratch?

options.t: Love it, give me a tutorial and I'm off
Okay if it looks simple enough
I'd rather pay an expert who already knows

questions.q: How do you feel about the cleanup, mess, and trips to the hardware store?

options.t: All part of the fun, I don't mind
Tolerable for the right project
That's exactly why I'd hire it out

results.title: You're a Call-a-Pro type, and that's totally fine
results.body: Your time, peace of mind, and a clean result matter more to you than the do-it-yourself badge, and there's real wisdom in knowing that. You don't have to become a weekend warrior to be a great homeowner. Start small: learning a few no-tools-needed basics (resetting a tripped breaker, plunging a drain, tightening a loose handle) can save you a service call without the stress. Everything bigger? Hand it off with confidence.
results.cta: Read our 'when to call a pro' guide

results.title: You're a Selective DIYer with room to grow
results.body: You've got the instinct and a few tools, you just pick your battles, and that's a smart way to fix things. With a little guidance you could confidently handle more of the small, safe jobs and save the pros for the ones that truly need them. Pick one beginner project, follow a step-by-step guide, and build from there.

results.title: You're a Confident DIYer through and through
results.body: Crooked hinges and stubborn faucets don't stand a chance, you've got the tools, the patience, and the itch to fix things yourself. Keep feeding that skill set with deeper tutorials and the right gear, and always pause before the big-risk jobs: gas, major electrical, and structural work still belong to a licensed pro, even for the handiest among us.
